Stage 2 assigns A+: that project-and-lineup combination merits actively making room during a Tokyo stay, while three nights and six sets, plus the absence of a world-premiere, farewell or terminal claim, make A+ sufficient rather than S. events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Kurt Rosenwinkel's COVER ZONE from March 11 through March 13, 2027, as the project's first Japanese presentation. March 11 and 12 have 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM sets; March 13 has 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM sets. Rosenwinkel appears with bassist Tim Lefebvre, keyboardist Jason Lindner, rhythm guitarist Matthew Rotker-Lynn and drummer Earl Harvin. The venue describes the project as new arrangements of familiar 1970s and 1980s songs, including music associated with Tears for Fears and Wham!, explored through reharmonization, rhythmic revision and improvisation. The music charge is ¥9,500, with seat-inclusive totals up to ¥15,000. Member reservations open December 8 at noon and general web reservations open December 15 at noon.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is not Rosenwinkel playing standards under a new title. COVER ZONE puts widely shared pop memory through a band built for harmonic and rhythmic disruption: Lefebvre and Lindner bring the low-end and keyboard chemistry heard on Bowie's Blackstar, while two guitars and Earl Harvin leave room for the songs to be rebuilt rather than merely covered. Its first Japanese presentation makes this specific configuration worth hearing.
en.trip_verdict: If a Tokyo stay overlaps March 11–13, actively make room for one of the six sets. The project and lineup are distinctive enough to choose over a routine club night, while the three-night run offers flexibility and does not justify reorganizing the trip around a single performance.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho no es escuchar a Rosenwinkel tocar standards bajo un título nuevo. COVER ZONE pasa una memoria pop compartida por una banda diseñada para alterar armonía y ritmo: Lefebvre y Lindner traen la química de bajo y teclados que se oyó en Blackstar de Bowie, mientras dos guitarras y Earl Harvin dejan espacio para reconstruir las canciones en vez de simplemente versionarlas. Que sea la primera presentación japonesa de esta configuración concreta le da valor propio.
es.trip_verdict: Si una estancia en Tokio coincide con el 11–13 de marzo, le haría espacio activamente a uno de los seis sets. El proyecto y la formación son suficientemente particulares para elegirlos sobre una noche rutinaria de club, mientras las tres noches dan flexibilidad y no justifican reorganizar el viaje alrededor de una sola función.
